mainTopic: Oil and לבונה on the מנחת חוטא; the משנה on הגשה and תנופה of מנחות; ten loaves of one kind; the source for הגשה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: the double word 'עליה' is a רבוי אחר רבוי, which only comes to limit. In a second version, רבי יוחנן asks whether a tiny bit of oil on a כזית of a מנחת חוטא counts, and the question ends in a תיקו. A ברייתא then teaches that 'עליה' refers to the מנחה itself. So one כהן who puts both oil and לבונה on it breaks two prohibitions, while setting a vessel on top of the מנחה's vessel does not make it פסול. A new משנה sorts מנחות into four groups by whether they need הגשה, תנופה, both, or neither. It lists the מנחות that need הגשה but not תנופה. רבי שמעון disagrees about the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח, saying that with no קמיצה there is no הגשה. In the גמרא, רב פפא rules that an oven-baked מנחה must be ten of one kind, rejecting רבי שמעון's half-and-half view. Finally, a ברייתא derives from the פסוק that the whole מנחה, including the מנחת חוטא, needs הגשה, and it begins asking whether logic alone could teach this. That argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two inclusions in a row only come to limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier answer: the double 'עליה' is a רבוי אחר רבוי, and that kind of double inclusion only comes to limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is one inclusion after another inclusion, and one inclusion after another inclusion only comes to limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an answer from just before this section. It says the word 'עליה' appears twice, once for oil and once for לבונה. That makes a 'רבוי אחר רבוי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a word that adds (a רבוי) widens the law. But there is a rule that when one רבוי comes right after another, together they narrow the law instead. That rule is what settles the earlier question about the מנחת חוטא.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion: a word in the פסוק that widens the law
One inclusion after another; by rule this comes to limit, not to widen
To exclude or limit

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards: two words that each add should add even more. The rule is the opposite. Two inclusions in a row work together to limit.

phrases.english: it is one inclusion after another inclusion,
phrases.notes: The two inclusions are the word 'עליה' said about the oil and 'עליה' said about the לבונה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רִבּוּי אַחַר רִבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט.
phrases.english: and one inclusion after another only comes to limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The double 'עליה' is a רבוי אחר רבוי, so it limits the law instead of widening it.

steps.title: Does a tiny bit of oil on a כזית count?
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבי יוחנן asks: if a tiny bit of oil was put on a כזית of the מנחה, is the prohibition broken? Must 'placing' oil follow the same rule as 'giving' לבונה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רב יצחק בר יוסף said that רבי יוחנן asked: if someone put any amount of oil on top of a כזית of a מנחה, what is the law? Do we require 'placing' to be like 'giving', or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the discussion. In this version, רבי יוחנן's question is about oil, not לבונה. He asks if even a tiny drop of oil on a כזית of the מנחה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two different verbs. It says 'לא ישים' (he shall not place) for oil and 'לא יתן' (he shall not give) for לבונה. The question is whether the oil rule copies the לבונה rule, which needs a כזית. If it does, a tiny drop of oil would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Any tiny amount
An olive-sized amount, a basic halachic measure
'Placing', the verb the פסוק uses for the oil
'Giving', the verb the פסוק uses for the לבונה
'What is the law?', the opening of a question

phrases.english: And there are those who say,
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said:
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
if he put any amount of oil
on top of an olive-bulk of a meal offering, what is the law?
Do we require 'placing' to be like 'giving'
phrases.notes: 'Placing' is the word used for oil and 'giving' is the word used for לבונה (ויקרא 5:11).

phrases.english: or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the discussion, with the question now about oil
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does even a tiny bit of oil on a כזית of a מנחת חוטא break the prohibition? Or must the oil rule match the כזית rule of the לבונה?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא could not find a source to settle רבי יוחנן's question. So it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיקו' means the question is left without a ruling. The גמרא does not decide whether 'placing' oil follows the rule of 'giving' לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand': the question is left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רבי יוחנן's question about a tiny bit of oil on a כזית is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 2 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of whether placing oil must match giving לבונה stays open.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: oil on the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about putting oil on the שיריים of the מנחה. It is setting up a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put oil on its leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This step only sets up the next move, the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that putting oil on the שיריים (the part left after the קומץ was taken) does not break the prohibition. The גמרא now brings a ברייתא that explains how the prohibition of 'עליה' works.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftovers of a מנחה after the קומץ is removed
The meal offering of a sinner, which may not have oil or לבונה

phrases.english: If he put oil on its leftovers,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting oil on the שיריים of the מנחה does not break the prohibition.

steps.title: The ברייתא suggests the rule might be about two כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes 'לא ישים עליה שמן ולא יתן'. It suggests the two separate prohibitions might apply only when two כהנים do the two acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'He shall not place oil on it, nor shall he give.' One might think this means two כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible but mistaken reading of the פסוק. It is setting up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the two prohibitions, oil and לבונה, might count separately only if one כהן put the oil and another put the לבונה. If so, one כהן who did both would get only one set of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a possible reading that will be rejected
Lashes, the punishment for breaking a Torah prohibition

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"He shall not place oil on it
nor shall he give",
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: 'any לבונה on it'.

phrases.english: one might think this is with two priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יָשִׂים עָלֶיהָ שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא יִתֵּן, יָכוֹל בִּשְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A possible reading: the two separate prohibitions apply only when two כהנים do the acts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the two separate prohibitions of oil and לבונה apply only when two different כהנים do the two acts, or also when one כהן does both?

steps.title: 'עליה' means the offering itself, not the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the two-כהנים reading. The word 'עליה' shows the פסוק is talking about the מנחה itself, not about the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'on it'. The פסוק is speaking about the meal offering itself, and not about the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own suggestion from the previous step. It uses the word 'עליה' to show that the rule depends on the offering, not on who does the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'עליה' is said about both the oil and the לבונה, both prohibitions are about the same מנחה. So even one כהן who puts both oil and לבונה on it breaks two prohibitions and gets two sets of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': brings the proof from the words of the פסוק
The meal offering itself
'The פסוק is speaking about'

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibitions of oil and לבונה are about the מנחה itself. One כהן who does both breaks two separate prohibitions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the number of prohibitions depends on what is done to the object, not on how many people do it.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "on it",
the verse is speaking about the meal offering itself,
and not about the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible reading from step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עליה' shows that the prohibitions are about the מנחה itself, not about the כהן. So one כהן who does both acts breaks two prohibitions.

steps.title: Maybe a vessel on top of a vessel also counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that setting a vessel of oil or לבונה on top of the vessel holding the מנחה might also be forbidden and might ruin the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: one may not put a vessel on top of a vessel, and if he did, he made the מנחה פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises one more possible reading of the פסוק. Maybe even putting a vessel of oil on top of the מנחה's vessel is forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 already used 'עליה' to show the פסוק talks about the מנחה, not the כהנים. Now the ברייתא tests a wider reading: maybe any closeness, even vessel on vessel, is forbidden. If so, it would also make the מנחה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think' — opens a possible reading that will be tested
A vessel on top of a vessel
He made it פסול (unfit to be offered)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יִתֵּן כְּלִי עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי,
phrases.english: You might think: one may not place a vessel on top of a vessel,
phrases.notes: He means a vessel holding oil or לבונה set on top of the vessel holding the מנחה.

phrases.english: and if he placed it, he made it unfit?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִתֵּן כְּלִי עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second 'יכול' in the same ברייתא, testing a wider reading of the prohibition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the prohibition of putting oil or לבונה on the מנחה include putting their vessel on the מנחה's vessel?

steps.title: 'Upon it' means the מנחה itself
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עליה' shows the prohibition is only about putting oil or לבונה directly on the מנחה, not vessel on vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'upon it.' The פסוק is speaking about the מנחה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the word 'עליה': only putting oil or לבונה on the מנחה itself is forbidden. A vessel on top of a vessel is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'עליה' does two jobs. In step 6 it showed the rule is about the מנחה and not about how many כהנים are involved. Here it limits the rule to direct contact with the מנחה's body, so a vessel on a vessel does not make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches' — brings the proof from the wording
'Upon it' — on the מנחה
On the body of the מנחה itself

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition of putting oil or לבונה on the מנחה applies only to the מנחה itself. A vessel resting on its vessel does not make it פסול.

phrases.english: The verse states: "upon it,"
the verse is speaking about the meal offering itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wider reading raised in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The prohibition is only about direct contact with the מנחה itself, as shown by 'עליה'.

steps.title: New משנה: four groups of מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sorts מנחות into four groups based on whether they need הגשה, תנופה, both, or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are some that need bringing near but not waving; some that need bringing near and waving; some that need waving but not bringing near; and some that need neither waving nor bringing near.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and gives a general outline of four groups of מנחות. The next lines will fill in which מנחות belong to each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate actions are in play: הגשה, bringing the מנחה to the corner of the מזבח, and תנופה, waving it. Since each can be present or missing, there are four possible combinations. The משנה names all four before giving details.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח
Waving the offering
Require; need

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה, וְאֵין טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה.
phrases.english: There are those that require bringing near but do not require waving.
Bringing near and waving.
Waving but not bringing near.
Neither waving nor bringing near.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה, וְאֵין טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחות fall into four groups: הגשה without תנופה, both, תנופה without הגשה, and neither.

steps.title: The מנחות that need הגשה but not תנופה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the first group: the ten kinds of מנחות that need הגשה but no תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These need bringing near but not waving: the fine-flour מנחה, the pan מנחה, the deep-pan מנחה, the loaves, the wafers, the מנחה of כהנים, the מנחה of the כהן משיח, the מנחה of gentiles, the מנחה of women, and the מנחה of a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts filling in its outline by listing which מנחות belong to the first group: הגשה but no תנופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list covers the regular voluntary מנחות, which are fine flour, מחבת, מרחשת, and the oven-baked kind as חלות or רקיקין. It also covers מנחות brought by special people: כהנים, the כהן משיח, gentiles, women, and the מנחת חוטא. According to this anonymous view, all of them need הגשה and none need תנופה.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain fine-flour מנחה
A flat pan / a deep pan, two ways of cooking a מנחה
Loaves / wafers, the two forms of an oven-baked מנחה
The anointed כהן גדול
The מנחה a poor sinner brings for certain sins

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה וְאֵין טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה:
phrases.english: And these require bringing near but do not require waving:
the fine-flour meal offering, the pan, and the deep pan,
and the loaves, and the wafers,
the meal offering of priests, and the meal offering of the anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת גּוֹיִם, מִנְחַת נָשִׁים, וּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: the meal offering of gentiles, the meal offering of women, and the meal offering of a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה וְאֵין טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the first of the four groups listed in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten kinds of מנחות need הגשה but not תנופה, including the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: no קמיצה means no הגשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח need no הגשה, since no קמיצה is taken from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the מנחה of כהנים and the מנחה of the כהן משיח do not need bringing near, because no handful is removed from them. Any מנחה with no handful removed has no bringing near.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the list in step 10 about two of its items. He takes them out of the הגשה group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון ties הגשה to קמיצה. A מנחת כהנים is burned whole on the מזבח, so no handful is removed from it. In his view, a מנחה with no קמיצה needs no הגשה either. The תנא קמא counts these two as needing הגשה anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a handful from the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Because
And any case where there is no... (a general rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח need הגשה. רבי שמעון says they do not, because in his view no קמיצה means no הגשה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying these are not real מנחות. He is only saying that the הגשה step does not apply to them, because no קמיצה is taken from them.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון's rule shows a link between two parts of the מנחה service: in his view, הגשה only exists where קמיצה exists.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest
do not have bringing near,
because they have no removal of a handful,
and any that have no removal of a handful
have no bringing near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with two items in the list of step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח need no הגשה, because any מנחה with no קמיצה has no הגשה.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'Ten' means ten of one kind
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states a rule: wherever the משנה says a מנחה comes as ten loaves, it means ten of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב פפא said: Wherever we learned [loaves or wafers], we learned ten of that one kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. רב פפא gives a general rule about how to read the number 'ten' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven-baked מנחה can be made of חלות (thick loaves) or רקיקין (thin wafers). רב פפא says that when the משנה requires ten, all ten must be one type: ten חלות or ten רקיקין, never a mix.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that explains the משנה
Ten, the number of loaves or wafers in certain מנחות

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Pappa said:
Anywhere that we learned [loaves or wafers], we learned ten [of that kind].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנַן עֶשֶׂר – תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה listed in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the משנה says a מנחה comes as ten, all ten must be of one type.

steps.title: What is רב פפא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point רב פפא's rule adds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this at all. This question sets up the next step, which explains whose view he is rejecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every statement must teach something new. It wants to know which opposing opinion רב פפא's rule comes to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asking what the new point is)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of רב פפא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion or possible mistake רב פפא's rule comes to rule out.

steps.title: רב פפא rejects רבי שמעון's half-and-half view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's rule excludes רבי שמעון, who allows bringing half חלות and half רקיקין. The משנה holds this is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude the view of רבי שמעון, who says: He may bring half loaves and half wafers. He teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא is rejecting רבי שמעון's opinion. According to the משנה, you cannot mix five חלות and five רקיקין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that one may split the ten into half חלות and half רקיקין. רב פפא tells us the תנא of our משנה disagrees: all ten must be one kind.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to rule out another opinion)
Thick loaves
Thin wafers
Half

steps.whatToRemember: According to our משנה, the ten loaves of a baked מנחה must be all חלות or all רקיקין. Only רבי שמעון allows half and half.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Shimon, who says:
He may bring half loaves and half wafers,
He teaches us that [he may] not.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא's rule rejects רבי שמעון's view that one may bring half חלות and half רקיקין.

steps.title: What is the source for הגשה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rules about which מנחות need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic: the משנה's list of מנחות that need הגשה. It asks where this comes from in the תורה, and this sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed מנחות that need הגשה, including the מנחת חוטא, and recorded רבי שמעון's view that the מנחת כהנים does not need it. The גמרא now wants the פסוק behind these rules.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב פפא's topic and goes back to the משנה's rules about הגשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches which מנחות need הגשה.

steps.title: Without the word 'מנחה,' only the קומץ would need הגשה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the פסוק had left out the word 'the מנחה,' we would think only the קומץ needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: If it had said 'And you shall bring that which is made of these to ה׳, and it shall be brought to the כהן, and he shall bring it near,' I would say: Only the קומץ needs הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It first imagines the פסוק without the words 'the מנחה' and shows what we would have thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without those words, the פסוק could be read as speaking only about the קומץ (the handful burned on the מזבח). This sets up the next step, where the extra words teach more.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח
The handful of the מנחה that is burned on the מזבח
I would have said (what we might have thought)
If it had said (imagining the פסוק worded differently)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר ״וְהֵבֵאתָ אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מֵאֵלֶּה לַה׳
phrases.english: If it had said: 'And you shall bring that which is made of these to the Lord,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8. The real פסוק says 'the מנחה' after 'And you shall bring'; the ברייתא imagines it without those words.

phrases.english: 'and it shall be brought to the priest, and he shall bring it near,'
I would say:
I only have [a source] that requires bringing near
for the handful alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's first stage: without the extra words, only the קומץ would need הגשה.

steps.title: The extra words include the whole מנחה and the מנחת חוטא
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מנחה' teaches that the whole מנחה needs הגשה. The fuller wording 'את המנחה' includes the מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn this about the whole מנחה? The פסוק says 'מנחה.' From where about the מנחת חוטא? The פסוק says 'את המנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer. Each extra word in the פסוק adds something that needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מנחה' shows that the whole מנחה, not just the קומץ, needs הגשה before the קומץ is taken. The fuller wording 'את המנחה' adds the מנחת חוטא as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the source)
The מנחה of a sinner, brought for certain sins
From where do we know?

steps.whatToRemember: From 'מנחה' we learn the whole מנחה needs הגשה. From 'את המנחה' we learn the מנחת חוטא also needs הגשה.

phrases.english: [That the whole] meal offering [needs it], from where?
The verse states: 'meal offering.'
The meal offering of a sinner, from where?
The verse states: 'the meal offering.'
phrases.notes: The fuller wording 'את המנחה', not just plain 'מנחה', is what adds the sinner's מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 16 and adds what the extra words teach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מנחה' includes the whole מנחה, and 'את המנחה' includes the מנחת חוטא, as needing הגשה.

steps.title: Couldn't we learn this through logic instead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the wording 'את המנחה' is needed to include the מנחת חוטא in הגשה, since it seems we could prove it with logic. It begins that logic by noting that 'bringing' is said about the מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this could be figured out by logic: 'bringing' is said here (about the מנחת חוטא)...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is challenging its own last derivation, asking whether we even need the wording 'את המנחה' to teach that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה. This line only sets up the logical argument; the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the ברייתא used the wording 'את המנחה' to include the מנחת חוטא in the rule of הגשה. Now it suggests that a פסוק may not be needed, because logic might prove the same thing. The starting point of the logic is that the תורה uses the word 'bring' (הבאה) for the מנחת חוטא, which will be compared to another מנחה where 'bring' is also said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it is logical': a way of saying we could learn this through reasoning, without a פסוק
A logical derivation or proof
'It is said': introduces a word the Torah uses in one place, to compare it with another place
'Bringing': the Torah's word for bringing the מנחה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying the מנחת חוטא is exempt from הגשה. It agrees it needs הגשה; it is only asking whether we need a פסוק to teach it, or whether logic is enough.

phrases.english: But it is logical
'Bringing' is stated here
phrases.notes: Here means the מנחת חוטא. The ברייתא is about to compare it to another מנחה where 'bringing' is also said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the פסוק-based inclusion from step 17 is needed, by proposing a logical derivation instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the wording 'את המנחה' to include the מנחת חוטא in the requirement of הגשה (step 17).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If logic can prove that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה, then the extra word in the פסוק would be unnecessary. The argument begins from the word 'bringing' being stated about the מנחת חוטא.
